title: The Day of the Two Blue Umbrellas
skyStory: A four percent eyelash is all that remains of the moon, still lounging in Aries and still eating the crackers. It has decided to spend its last light on mischief. Somewhere tonight two things that should never match will match perfectly, and the moon will claim it planned the whole thing. Saturn checks the paperwork. The signature is in crayon, but it is valid.

reading: Something odd is lined up for you around 11:20. You will think of a word you have not said in years, maybe periwinkle, maybe gazebo, and within the hour someone will say it out loud in a completely unrelated sentence. Don't even scream. Just raise one eyebrow, slowly, like a detective in the rain.

The Aries moon is still sprawled across your couch, so your energy stays high but scattered. Take a breath before you answer anything with an exclamation point. The [[Eight of Swords]] reversed reminds you that most cages today are just tape on the floor. Step over them.
joel.mission: Pick an odd word right now and drop it into one conversation today without explaining yourself.
joel.omen: Two strangers carrying matching blue umbrellas on a dry day. You and Nancy are about to think the same thought.
joel.stoneWhy: a clear signal through the noise

reading: Your Life Path 11 is buzzing like a porch light full of moths. Little patterns jump out: a licence plate with your birthday digits, the same song in two different shops, a cat in a window that looks exactly like a cat from grade four.

Write them down as they come. By supper you will have a list of three, and the third will connect to something Joel says tonight in a way that makes you both put your phones down and stare at the ceiling. The Wood Rat saw it coming, of course. The Wood Rat always sees it coming.
nancy.mission: Keep a tally of every coincidence you notice today on a sticky note, and send Joel the final count.
nancy.omen: A delivery van with your initials painted on the side. Not a sign. Okay, a little bit a sign.

together.text: ΔΕΣ is on the menu. Before bed, each of you write down the strangest match of the day, then reveal at the same moment. If they connect, you owe the moon a thank-you wave out the window. If they don't, wave anyway. It worked hard.

game.intro: DES alert: two blue umbrellas, one sidewalk. Saturn wants to know if your brains match as well as your gear.
game.question: You open an umbrella you forgot you owned and something falls out. What do you hope it is?
options: A note in your own handwriting
A key to nothing you own
